# SOP-204 — Conveyor Belt Safety Inspection

**Applies to:** Overland conveyor systems C-1 through C-6, bulk material handling area.

## 1. Inspection Interval

A safety walk-down inspection is required every shift (8 hours). A
detailed mechanical inspection (belt tracking, idler condition, tensioning,
emergency-stop function) is required weekly.

## 2. Standard Operating Parameters

- Normal belt speed: 2.1 - 2.6 meters per second.
- Maximum allowable belt sway (tracking deviation): 50 millimeters from
  centerline at any idler station.
- Emergency pull-cord response time: must stop the belt within 2 seconds
  of activation.
- Maximum ambient dust concentration at transfer points: 5 mg/m3.

## 3. Alert Thresholds Requiring Escalation

- Belt tracking deviation exceeding 75 millimeters at any station.
- Emergency-stop response time exceeding 3 seconds during weekly test.
- Any exposed or damaged guarding around nip points.
- Belt slip exceeding 5% under normal load, indicating tensioning or
  drive-drum wear issues.
- Smoke, burning odor, or elevated drive-motor temperature above 95
  degrees Celsius.

## 4. Corrective Actions

- Tracking deviation: adjust training idlers; if deviation persists after
  adjustment, inspect for structural misalignment.
- Emergency-stop failure: take the conveyor out of service immediately
  and notify electrical maintenance — this is a stop-work condition, not
  a scheduled-maintenance item.
- Belt slip: inspect and re-tension the take-up unit; check drive drum
  lagging wear.

## 5. Approval

Any stop-work condition (Section 4, emergency-stop failure) requires
sign-off from both the shift supervisor and a safety officer before the
conveyor is restarted.
